Heater Shield.Notes:
Shields requires you to be out of combat to equip or unequip.
Dual wielding Shields requires a Feat.
You can't use Two-Handed Weapons with a Shield.
Any Hero can freely wear a Shield, as long as the Stat requirements are met. While wearing a Shield, you can't use Two-Handed Weapons, but you can use 1-Action Abilities normally.
Heater Shield.Name: Heater Shield

Tower Shield.Notes:
Remember that you have to declare whether you have a Shield equipped when you start your turn!
Dual wielding Shields requires a Feat.
You can't use Two-Handed Weapons with a Shield.
Tower Shield.Name: Tower Shield

Unarmored.Notes: No armor or very little clothing, such as a bare chest or lightly clothed body. You rely on your reflexes more than on armor.
Unarmored.Name: Unarmored

Robes.EffectGreen: You have 1 extra Level 1 Utility or Class Talent.
Robes.Notes: Robes vary in purpose and design. They can symbolize a wizard's robes, a priest's apparel or a noble's dress.
Robes.Name: Robes

Leather Armor.Notes: The breastplate and shoulder protectors of this armor are made of leather that has been stiffened by being boiled in oil.
Leather Armor.Name: Leather Armor

Hide Armor.EffectGreen:
+2 Max Health
You can move through spaces of Enemies.
Hide Armor.Notes: Hide armor is crafted from multiple layers of toughened skins, typically harvested from thick-hided creatures like cattle, bears, or similar animals. Unlike a stiff breastplate, the hides are naturally articulated and allow for softer brushing against the various battlefield combatants.
Hide Armor.Name: Hide Armor

Cuirass.EffectGreen: You Heal for 10% of all melee Damage you deal (rounded down) in a Worthy Combat.
Cuirass.Notes: A Cuirass consists of a light chestpiece made of leather and metal, with a tasset cover for the upper legs. This is an armor type favored by gladiators, barbarians and other hand-to-hand fighters who are not afraid of blood, be it theirs or their enemies'. The thrill of battle and spill of blood invigorates the wearer.
Cuirass.Name: Cuirass

Ring Mail.Notes: Unlike standard chainmail, which features a complex weave of interlocking rings, ring mail is a simpler form of flexible armor consisting of metal rings sewn or riveted directly onto a heavy garment made of leather or quilted fabric.
Ring Mail.Name: Ring Mail

Lorica.Notes: A lorica consists of horizontal iron strips fastened together by internal leather straps. The construction style differs from lorica to lorica, resembling chain mail, smallplate or shortscale. These suits are engineered to offer a high degree of protection against both blunt force and piercing weapons while remaining flexible enough for the wearer to move effectively in formation.
Lorica.Name: Lorica

Combat Extras: -50% Slam, Pulse, Cold, Fall Damage taken
Padded Armor.EffectGreen:
-50% taken Slam collision, Pulse, Cold and falling Damage by 50%.
You are immune to being Pushed.
Padded Armor.Upgrade: The Slam Damage Reduction applies to the collision Units as well!
Padded Armor.Notes:
Padded Armor consists of quilted layers of cloth and batting. Its thickness is great for absorbing heavy blunt hits... and for when you fall off a cliff. It happens to the best of us.
Alternatives: Hide Armor (resistance to Cold Damage instead of Pulse).
Padded Armor.Name: Padded Armor

Half-Plate.Notes: Half-plate is a suit of armor that covers the most vital parts of the body, while leaving the lower limbs largely unprotected to favor mobility and reduced weight. It is constructed from large, shaped steel plates that are heat-treated for hardness and joined together by internal leather straps and sliding rivets.
Half-Plate.Name: Half-Plate

Splint Armor.Notes: This armor is made of narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a backing of leather that is worn over cloth padding. Flexible Chain Mail protects the joints, providing great overall protection.
Splint Armor.Name: Splint Armor

Chain Mail.Notes: Made of interlocking metal rings, Chain Mail includes a layer of quilted fabric worn underneath the heavy mail to prevent chafing and to cushion the impact of blows, making wounds received this way not only lighter, but also much faster to Heal.
Chain Mail.Name: Chain Mail

Bastion Plate.EffectGreen:
+1 Health Regen
If you didn't move from place last Turn, you gain +2 meters Range and your first attack this Turn ignores Cover. The Range bonus stacks!
Bastion Plate.Upgrade: The Range bonus is lost and resets after moving from place.
Bastion Plate.Name: Bastion Plate

Brigandine.EffectGreen: You can move 1 meter for free each Turn.
Brigandine.Notes: A heavy brigandine is a piece of body armor consisting of many small steel plates riveted to a heavy leather fabric, allowing for enhanced mobility, but requiring more torque in order to get going.
Brigandine.Name: Brigandine

Plate Armor.Notes: Plate consists of shaped, interlocking metal plates to cover the entire body. A suit of plate includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, a visored helmet, and thick layers of padding underneath the armor. Buckles and straps distribute the weight over the body. However, the weight of the armor makes it difficult to hold still and aim at range.
Plate Armor.Name: Plate Armor

Scale Mail.Requirement: 2 or more Might and Worthy Combat
Scale Mail.EffectGreen: If you end your Turn with unspend {A}Action Points, gain 2 1d4 Shieldings.
Scale Mail.Notes: This armor consists of a coat and leggings (and perhaps a separate skirt) of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish.
Scale Mail.Name: Scale Mail
